When did you come with the second thing that's jazz music?
Oh, I guess I can almost remember that from the time I was a child that noticed anything, when I first took an interest in it, I suppose, like most kids of today, was when I was in my early teens.
Well, when you first heard it as a child, did you hear any opinions expressed on it, like by your parents or friends of your parents?

I don't remember my parents talking about it so much when I was a child. But when I became about maybe 15 or 16 years old and we got a vitro and some of us started buying jazz records and bringing them home, I can remember my mother thought they were perfectly awful. She liked good music and always had and just didn't care for the jazz. What did you mean classical music? She was interested in classical music only and I'd say to this day is interested in classical music only. Now, my father was tone deaf, so he always said, and any music, whether it's good or bad, always seemed to racket to him. So it didn't seem to matter much whether it was opera or Dixieland jazz. All of them he didn't care for.
Well, what about the friends of your parents? Did any of them say anything good in the music?

I don't remember many friends of my parents even discussing jazz to any extent. I know that we all liked Dixieland jazz when I started going to dances and things. You and your friends? Our friends. We all loved it. Oh, we liked Papa Celestine who was probably in his glory then and better then than he is even now. What about what did you say? Oh, well, I would say in about, oh, the late 20s and early 30s. I can remember Papa Celestine playing Hold That Tiger and how we danced well around. We didn't jitterbug in those years. Now, a few years later after I was married, the jitterbug came into being. But before that we did the Charleston and a few things like that. And we loved Dixieland jazz. And frankly, I think we danced a lot more to it than it was real dancing and had a rhythm and a beat much better than the music that you are nowadays.
And then it was very popular with your set. Oh, oh, yes. How about what age?

Well, now let me see. It goes back a little. I'd say around 1930, all of us were dancing to Dixieland jazz.
